chunks.label: What shop staff say
chunks.rationale: Lets you recognise the greetings and replies staff use every time you buy or order.
chunks.interference: Gochuumon and okoshi are staff words; for yourself say chuumon and ukagaimasu.

chunks.label: Hungry tasty and full
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about hunger and food before, during and after a meal.
chunks.interference: Oishisou is before eating, oishikatta after; tabesugita and mou taberarenai both mean you're full but only the second refuses more.

chunks.label: Choosing what to buy
chunks.rationale: Lets you pick an item, ask for advice and try clothes on.
chunks.interference: Kore kudasai points at a thing; kore ni shimasu announces a decision after comparing.
members: 試着してもいいですか

chunks.label: Price and paying
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask the price, check the tax and pay by card.
chunks.interference: Kaado tsukaemasu ka asks if cards work; kaado de onegai shimasu chooses card.
members: カードでお願いします
レシートは大丈夫です

chunks.label: Bags and wrapping
chunks.rationale: Lets you answer the bag and wrapping questions at every till.
chunks.interference: Daijoubu desu here means no thanks, not yes.

chunks.label: Asking restaurant staff
chunks.rationale: Lets you get seated, order, ask for water and the toilet, and finish ordering.
chunks.interference: Ijou desu ends your order; it doesn't ask for the bill.

chunks.label: Eat in or take out
chunks.rationale: Lets you answer the counter's eat-in question and size up a bowl.
chunks.interference: Tennai de is eating here, mochikaeri de is taking it away.

chunks.label: Asking if it's okay
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask permission, from casual to very polite.
chunks.interference: Ii desu ka asks permission; ii no? checks someone means their offer.

chunks.label: Deciding what to do
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask what to do, agree on a plan and say you don't mind.
chunks.interference: Dou suru? asks what we'll do; dou shitara ii? asks for advice when stuck.

chunks.label: Offering things and help
chunks.rationale: Lets you offer food, a turn or a hand without pressure.
chunks.interference: Ikaga desu ka offers politely; douzo douzo hands over or lets someone go first.
members: 何かあったら言ってね

chunks.label: Accepting kindness
chunks.rationale: Lets you accept an offer or gift gracefully.
chunks.interference: Ki o tsukawanaide sounds like a refusal but still ends in accepting.

chunks.label: Turning things down
chunks.rationale: Lets you say no politely without a long excuse.
chunks.interference: Kekkou desu is a firm no; enryo shite okimasu and kyou wa chotto are softer.

chunks.label: Asking a favour
chunks.rationale: Lets you open a request and ask for help, casual or polite.
chunks.interference: Choudai and chotto tetsudatte are for close people; onegai dekimasu ka is the safe polite one.
members: お願いがあるんだけど

chunks.label: Leaving without buying
chunks.rationale: Lets you browse and walk away from a shop politely.
chunks.interference: Chotto kangaemasu usually means no, not a real maybe.

chunks.label: Drinking together
chunks.rationale: Lets you toast, order rounds and groan about it later.
chunks.interference: Mou ippai is one more drink; ippai alone also means full.

chunks.label: Paying the bill
chunks.rationale: Lets you treat someone, ask for the bill, a receipt or separate payment.
chunks.interference: Ryoushuusho is the formal expense receipt, not the till slip (reshiito).

chunks.label: Inviting someone to eat
chunks.rationale: Lets you suggest a drink, a meal or a coffee and plan what to eat.
chunks.interference: Gohan ikanai? is eating out; nani taberu? is choosing the food.

chunks.label: Counting on someone
chunks.rationale: Lets you lean on someone, plead with them, and promise to deliver.
chunks.interference: Tanomu yo asks for help; tanomu kara begs someone to stop or act.

chunks.label: Meals at home
chunks.rationale: Lets you call people to the table, serve them and offer seconds.
chunks.interference: Meshiagare is said by the cook; the eater says itadakimasu.

chunks.label: Office set phrases
chunks.rationale: Lets you handle the fixed greetings of work calls, emails and coming back to the office.
chunks.interference: Tadaima modorimashita is for the office; at home it's just tadaima.
members: お世話になっております

drops.reason: Duplicate of どうしたらいい？ (same phrase without the question mark).
Dictionary form of お腹すいた; the phrase is said as onaka suita, and onaka suiteru? is covered in that entry's notes.
The word inside いかがですか; that entry covers it and notes ikaga deshou ka and ikaga deshita ka.
